title: Rav Seuram or Seorim, Rava’s Brother
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Bava Metzia 73b mentions him compelling ill-behaved men to carry Rava’s palanquin. Rava tells him, “You did well.”

Moed Katan 28a [Hyman cites 28b] relates that Rav Seuram was present when Rava died. Rava asked him to tell the Angel of Death not to cause him pain. After his death, Rava appeared to Rav Seuram and said that dying had hurt only like bloodletting.

notes.text: The matching death dialogue is Moed Katan28a, though the notice cites28b. Rava is the deceased person who later appears to Seorim, not the reverse. The earlier clause concerns compelling people to carry a palanquin, not confiscating objects. The locator remains a source question.

No new primary scalar was supplied here. The earlier Moed Katan 28a death-dialogue consultation is inherited beside supplied כח: (28b). Rava is the deceased who appears to Seuram after death, not the recipient of Seuram's posthumous appearance. The Bava Metzia clause concerns compelling ill-behaved people to carry Rava's palanquin, not confiscating objects. Seuram/Seorim are heading alternatives, not newly bound identities. The Angel of Death expansion is contextual, and the bloodletting comparison is retained without adding a modern medical interpretation.

Hyman’s print cites Moed Katan 28b. The matching dialogue at 28a calls him Rav Seorim, Rava’s brother. Seorim asks Rava to appear to him, and Rava does so after his death. Rava likens the pain to the prick of a bloodletting blade. Bava Metzia 73b reads Seuram and gives Rava’s approval of the palanquin incident.
